dedupe_keys.name: usarray magnetotelluric transfer functions emtf database long period mt impedances at the 70 km emscope grid across the us and community sites

description: The EMTF database holds magnetotelluric transfer functions, the frequency-dependent impedances that describe how the ground's electrical conductivity turns magnetic variations into electric fields. EarthScope's data product portal, read on 2026-09-28, describes transfer functions calculated at the USArray magnetotelluric sites installed by Oregon State University plus other community sites, with a map and a table filterable by site, project, survey, quality, location, time and period range, all oriented to geographic coordinates with original orientations kept, documented by Kelbert and colleagues in 2018 and exchanged in the EMTF XML format with conversion utilities. The 2009 EMScope paper explains the origin: a 70 kilometre grid of long-period stations across the United States under the NSF EarthScope programme, with data openly available without charge or restriction. Coverage is the contiguous United States, with other community surveys. Access is free, and per-survey data citations are requested; no formal licence was read on the portal. Caveats: coverage and quality vary by survey and some sites may be unreleased. It supports space weather risk studies of power grids, such as computing geoelectric fields along transmission lines to estimate geomagnetically induced currents for a storm. Related records: NOAA geoelectric storm simulations, the Alberta 2023 GIC validation data and the IMAGE magnetometer network.
